Recent graduate (M.Ent.) from Carnegie Mellon University with prior professional experience in film and television before transitioning into human-computer interaction and immersive media research. My work investigates how AI, implicit interaction, and computational systems can expand cinematic language and reshape audience engagement in XR experiences. I combine expertise in narrative design, creative production, and user-centered research to develop interactive storytelling systems informed by HCI, machine learning, and cognitive science.

Research Experience

XR Researcher

Entertainment Technology Center, Carnegie Mellon University
Sep 2025 – Jul 2026

Project: Anamnesis, implicit interaction and narrative engagement in immersive film. PI: Prof. Vivian Shen.

  • Led a research collaboration with Vivian Shen, Abigail Noyce and Geoff Kaufman on how implicit interaction shapes audience engagement in immersive storytelling.
  • Designed a diegetic interface for a 270° C.A.V.E. that infers attention from head orientation and reveals hidden narrative layers without on-screen prompts.
  • Built an explicit, Bandersnatch-style baseline for the same film to isolate the interface from the narrative.
  • Wrote the IRB protocol; recruited, screened and ran all sessions of an exploratory study (N = 11) combining EEG with semi-structured interviews.
  • Ran a five-participant EEG pilot distinguishing four attention states (idle, seeking, found, recall); published at SIGGRAPH 2026.
  • Worked with neuroscience researchers on EEG signal processing and attention-state classification; coded interviews and ran band-power analysis.
  • Secured a CS+X grant (Frank-Ratchye STUDIO for Creative Inquiry) and an EEG headset for the study.

UX Researcher & Producer

Kicks Lab, Carnegie Mellon University
Sep 2025 – Jan 2026

STEM learning platform that teaches engineering through footwear, built with external client Ansys and partner Zellerfeld.

  • Managed a multidisciplinary collaboration between CMU, Ansys and Zellerfeld.
  • Led the UX research: ran playtest sessions with middle and high school students at a Pittsburgh charter school, measuring usability, motivation and comprehension of the STEM concepts.
  • Playtests showed students could reach the target by trial-and-error stat matching without engaging with the material science; added an estimation step that turns the loop into hypothesis-and-test.
  • Led production planning across research, design and engineering teams.
  • Project nominated for the UX Design Awards 2026.

Independent Researcher / Creator

Studio Isora
2026 – present

Research question: can a spatially grounded workflow let filmmakers use generative video without sacrificing creative control?

  • Ran a controlled study of compositional control across four AI image-generation pipelines on a six-shot test film, measuring each against the director’s locked frame.
  • Found that reference-image editors recompose the frame in roughly 80% of cases, while depth-conditioned generation holds it reliably at about a third of the cost.
  • Built the research apparatus: a desktop app that takes a script to a storyboard through in-scan camera framing in Gaussian-splat scans of real locations, with per-shot render history and provenance.
  • Developed supporting tools for the study: depth and edge map generation, composition-locked rendering, masked fill, and AI rotoscoping and subject removal.
